newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down at noon on worse sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down at noon on worse sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were down slightly at midday on Monday on worsening market sentiment, dampened by falls in A shares and rumours of further crackdown measures, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.307 points or 0.37 percent to 82.080 points on volume of 4.042 million shares worth $3.1 million.
The A index shed 30.649 points 2.34 percent to 1,279.978 points on turnover of 4.50 billion yuan.
According to the rumours, the government is planning to punish around 23 brokerages which contributed to volatile trading during market surges earlier this year, brokers said.
"The rumours about further crackdown measures depressed market sentiment, with some institutions seen offsetting their positions," brokers said.
"Retail investors were also cautious given the market uncertainties," he said.
"The index will test the 80-point support in the short term, with the technical charts showing signs of a downward trend," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 34 traded, with 20 down, four flat and 10 up.
Shanghai Jintai was the biggest loser on its poor prospects, slipping $0.014 or 8.74 percent to $0.146 on thin volume of 26,000 shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the most actively traded on institutional support, gaining $0.014 or 1.03 percent to $1.370 on volume of 565,500 shares.
Shanghai's A share index was sharply down on investors' jitters over possible crackdown measures, brokers said.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 73.772 points or 1.90 percent to 3,808.156 points.
